natural: years and months are quiet and good

meaning.en: A peaceful, untroubled life in which time passes calmly.
meaning.zh: 日子平静安稳，没有风波。

examples.zh: 他只希望一家人岁月静好，平平安安。
examples.en: All he hopes for is a calm, safe life for his family.

examples.zh: 退休后，她过上了岁月静好的生活。
examples.en: After retirement she has lived a calm and peaceful life.

usage.en: Often paired with 现世安稳; used as predicate or attributive. Sometimes used ironically of people who ignore hardships elsewhere.
usage.zh: 常与“现世安稳”连用，作谓语或定语；有时也反讽对他人苦难视而不见的人。

antonyms: 华北之大，已经安放不得一张平静的书桌了

literal: dare · be angry · not · dare · speak
natural: dare to be angry but not to speak

meaning.en: To feel anger but not dare to say anything, out of fear of the powerful.
meaning.zh: 心里愤怒，但因为害怕而不敢说出来。

examples.zh: 员工对新规定敢怒不敢言。
examples.en: Staff are angry about the new rules but dare not say so.

examples.zh: 面对恶霸，村民们只能敢怒不敢言。
examples.en: Faced with the bully, the villagers could only fume in silence.

usage.en: Used as predicate or adverbial; implies a power imbalance.
usage.zh: 作谓语或状语，暗含权势压迫。

natural: go back and weave a net

meaning.en: Rather than just wishing for something, go back and prepare practically for it.
meaning.zh: 与其空想，不如回去做好准备、踏实行动。

examples.zh: 想要好成绩，就该退而结网，认真复习。
examples.en: If you want good grades, stop wishing and review properly.

examples.zh: 临渊羡鱼不如退而结网，他开始学做生意。
examples.en: Rather than envying fish by the pool, he went back to prepare and started learning how to do business.

story.en: Dong Zhongshu is quoted: 'rather than standing at the pool and longing for fish, it is better to go back and weave a net' (临渊羡鱼，不如退而结网).
story.zh: 《汉书·董仲舒传》：“临川羡鱼，不如退而结网。”

usage.en: A piece of advice, usually after quoting 临渊羡鱼. Used as predicate.
usage.zh: 劝勉语，常接在“临渊羡鱼”之后，作谓语。

natural: a blade that cuts a hair blown across it

meaning.en: Describes an extremely sharp blade.
meaning.zh: 形容刀剑极其锋利，吹一根毛发过去也能割断。

equivalents: sharp enough to split a hair

examples.zh: 这柄古剑吹毛断发，是难得的宝物。
examples.en: This ancient sword is razor-sharp and a rare treasure.

examples.zh: 匠人把菜刀磨得吹毛断发。
examples.en: The craftsman honed the kitchen knife to razor sharpness.

usage.en: Literary; used as predicate or attributive, mostly about swords and knives.
usage.zh: 文言色彩，作谓语或定语，多形容刀剑。

natural: lie down on a peaceful pillow

meaning.en: To sleep soundly with no worries.
meaning.zh: 放心地躺下睡觉，形容毫无忧虑。

examples.zh: 边境安宁，百姓才能安枕而卧。
examples.en: Only when the border is calm can the people sleep in peace.

examples.zh: 账目都核对清楚了，他这才安枕而卧。
examples.en: Once the accounts were checked, he could finally rest easy.

usage.en: Used as predicate; usually after a threat has been removed. Close to 高枕无忧.
usage.zh: 作谓语，多用于危险消除之后，与“高枕无忧”相近。

natural: soldiers turn as the general turns

meaning.en: The troops follow their commander; a team's quality depends on its leader.
meaning.zh: 士兵跟着将领行动，比喻下属的表现取决于领导。

examples.zh: 兵随将转，球队换了教练后面貌一新。
examples.en: The troops follow the commander; the team looked transformed under the new coach.

examples.zh: 兵随将转，部门风气全看主管怎么带。
examples.en: Staff follow their leader, so the department's culture depends on how the manager leads.

usage.en: Often said of teams and organisations. Used as comment or predicate.
usage.zh: 多用于团队、组织，作评语或谓语。

natural: harmonise and regulate yin and yang

meaning.en: To harmonise yin and yang; said of a chief minister who governs the state well.
meaning.zh: 调和阴阳，旧指宰相辅佐君主，治理国家。

examples.zh: 宰相的职责在于燮理阴阳，安定天下。
examples.en: The chancellor's duty is to harmonise yin and yang and keep the realm stable.

examples.zh: 他位居三公，燮理阴阳，深得朝野敬重。
examples.en: As one of the Three Excellencies, he harmonised the state and won respect at court and beyond.

usage.en: Archaic and formal; mostly seen in historical writing about ministers.
usage.zh: 古雅、正式，多见于历史文章中关于宰辅的叙述。

natural: when cold, one does not choose one's clothes

meaning.en: When in dire need, one cannot afford to be choosy.
meaning.zh: 非常寒冷时顾不上挑选衣服，比喻处境窘迫时不暇选择。

examples.zh: 寒不择衣，我现在有工作就行，哪还挑什么待遇。
examples.en: Beggars can't be choosers; at the moment any job will do, never mind the pay.

examples.zh: 急着用钱，只能寒不择衣，先借了再说。
examples.en: Needing money urgently, I couldn't be picky and borrowed it first.

usage.en: Often paired with 饥不择食 and 慌不择路. Used as predicate or comment.
usage.zh: 常与“饥不择食”“慌不择路”并用，作谓语或评语。

natural: regard harmony as most precious

meaning.en: To value harmony above all and avoid conflict.
meaning.zh: 以和睦相处为最宝贵，避免冲突。

examples.zh: 邻里之间应以和为贵，别为小事争吵。
examples.en: Neighbours should value harmony and not argue over trifles.

examples.zh: 谈判时双方都表示以和为贵，愿意让步。
examples.en: In the negotiations both sides said they valued harmony and were willing to compromise.

story.en: The Analects records Youzi saying that in the practice of ritual, harmony is the most valuable thing (礼之用，和为贵), from which this expression developed.
story.zh: 《论语·学而》载有子曰：“礼之用，和为贵。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国初 · 前5—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to early Warring States, 5th–4th c. BC

usage.en: A maxim of Chinese social culture; used as predicate or motto. Based on the Analects' 礼之用，和为贵.
usage.zh: 中国社会文化的格言，作谓语或口号；出自《论语》“礼之用，和为贵”。

natural: wind like knives and frost like swords

meaning.en: Bitterly cold weather, or, figuratively, harsh and cruel circumstances.
meaning.zh: 形容严寒的气候，也比喻险恶、严酷的环境。

examples.zh: 北方的冬天风刀霜剑，出门要裹得严严实实。
examples.en: Winter in the north is bitterly cold, so one has to wrap up well to go out.

examples.zh: 她独自在风刀霜剑般的环境中长大。
examples.en: She grew up alone in harsh and unforgiving circumstances.

origin.source: 清·曹雪芹《红楼梦》第二十七回

story.en: In the 'Song of Burying Flowers', Lin Daiyu laments that 'three hundred and sixty days a year, wind-knives and frost-swords press hard' (一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼).
story.zh: 《红楼梦》第二十七回《葬花吟》：“一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼。”

date.en: Qing dynasty, mid-18th c. (first eighty chapters)

usage.en: Literary; used attributively or as predicate. Famously used in Lin Daiyu's poem about her fate.
usage.zh: 文学性强，作定语或谓语；因黛玉《葬花吟》而知名。

natural: racing horses and cockfighting

meaning.en: Idle amusements such as horse racing and cockfighting; leading an idle, frivolous life.
meaning.zh: 赛马、斗鸡，泛指游手好闲、纵情玩乐的生活。

examples.zh: 他整天走马斗鸡，不务正业。
examples.en: He spends his days on idle pastimes and neglects his proper work.

examples.zh: 小说里的纨绔子弟个个走马斗鸡，挥霍无度。
examples.en: In the novel the idle young nobles all squander their days on amusements.

usage.en: Used as predicate; implies dissipation. 斗鸡走狗 is a close relative.
usage.zh: 作谓语，含游手好闲之意，与“斗鸡走狗”相近。

natural: lay down arms and stop fighting

meaning.en: To end hostilities and make peace.
meaning.zh: 停止战争，结束交战。

examples.zh: 两国最终息兵罢战，开始和谈。
examples.en: The two countries finally stopped fighting and began peace talks.

examples.zh: 百姓都盼着息兵罢战，过上安稳日子。
examples.en: The people hoped for an end to the war so they could live in peace.

usage.en: Formal; used as predicate, usually in historical or political contexts.
usage.zh: 正式语，作谓语，多用于历史或政治语境。

natural: a mediocre doctor kills people

meaning.en: An incompetent doctor can kill; a warning about unqualified practitioners and misdiagnosis.
meaning.zh: 医术不高明的医生会害死人。

equivalents: a bad doctor is a menace

examples.zh: 庸医杀人，看病一定要找正规医院。
examples.en: An incompetent doctor can kill, so always go to a proper hospital.

examples.zh: 这起医疗事故被媒体称为庸医杀人。
examples.en: The press called this medical accident a case of a doctor killing through incompetence.

usage.en: A warning, also used in news headlines; as subject or comment.
usage.zh: 警示语，也见于新闻标题，作主语或评语。

natural: one mind with two uses

meaning.en: To do two things at once with one's attention divided, so that neither is done well.
meaning.zh: 同时做两件事，注意力不集中。

equivalents: try to do two things at once

examples.zh: 你别一心二用，吃饭的时候别看手机。
examples.en: Don't divide your attention; don't look at your phone while eating.

examples.zh: 他一心二用，作业和游戏都没做好。
examples.en: He tried to do two things at once, and did neither his homework nor the game well.

usage.en: Usually mildly critical; used as predicate. Contrasts with 专心致志.
usage.zh: 多带批评意味，作谓语，与“专心致志”相对。

natural: empty mouth, plain words

meaning.en: Mere talk with no proof or action behind it.
meaning.zh: 只说话，没有证据或行动作为凭据。

examples.zh: 空口白话谁都会说，拿出证据来。
examples.en: Anyone can talk; show me the evidence.

examples.zh: 他只是空口白话，从未兑现过承诺。
examples.en: It was just empty words; he has never kept a promise.

usage.en: Colloquial; used as attributive or comment. A close relative of 空口无凭, which stresses the lack of proof.
usage.zh: 口语，作定语或评语；与“空口无凭”相近，后者强调没有凭证。

natural: without applying powder or eyebrow pigment

meaning.en: Without makeup; having a natural, unadorned face.
meaning.zh: 不涂脂抹粉，素面朝天。

examples.zh: 她不施粉黛，却依然清丽动人。
examples.en: She wears no makeup yet still looks fresh and lovely.

examples.zh: 演员素颜出镜，不施粉黛，反而更自然。
examples.en: The actress appeared without makeup and looked all the more natural.

usage.en: Often used in praise of natural beauty. Used as predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 常用于称赞天然之美，作谓语或状语。

natural: lightly brushing the moth-like eyebrows

meaning.en: To wear only light makeup, accentuating only the eyebrows; understated elegance.
meaning.zh: 只淡淡地画一下眉毛，形容化妆朴素淡雅。

examples.zh: 她淡扫蛾眉，只涂了一点口红就出门了。
examples.en: She lightly darkened her eyebrows and went out with just a touch of lipstick.

examples.zh: 画中美人淡扫蛾眉，清雅脱俗。
examples.en: The beauty in the painting has lightly pencilled brows and an elegant, unworldly air.

story.en: Zhang Hu writes that Lady Guoguo, disdaining rouge that would sully her natural complexion, 'lightly brushed her eyebrows and went to see the Emperor' (却嫌脂粉污颜色，淡扫蛾眉朝至尊).
story.zh: 张祜《集灵台》：“却嫌脂粉污颜色，淡扫蛾眉朝至尊。”

date.en: Tang dynasty, first half of the 9th c.

usage.en: Literary, nearly always about women's makeup. Quoted from a Tang poem about Lady Guoguo.
usage.zh: 文学性强，多形容女子淡妆；出自咏虢国夫人的唐诗。

natural: effort is never wasted

meaning.en: Effort is never in vain; hard work always brings some reward.
meaning.zh: 努力不会白费，付出总有回报。

examples.zh: 功不唐捐，他坚持练习三年，终于获奖。
examples.en: Effort is never wasted: he practised for three years and finally won a prize.

examples.zh: 别灰心，功不唐捐，总会有收获的。
examples.en: Don't lose heart; no effort is wasted and you will reap something in the end.

usage.en: Literary encouragement; used as a maxim or predicate. 唐捐 means 'thrown away in vain'.
usage.zh: 文言劝勉语，作格言或谓语；“唐捐”指白白丢弃。

natural: Heaven does not lend more years

meaning.en: Heaven did not grant a longer life; said of someone who died too young.
meaning.zh: 上天不给他更长的寿命，指人早逝。

examples.zh: 天不假年，这位天才画家三十岁便去世了。
examples.en: Heaven did not grant him more years, and the gifted painter died at thirty.

examples.zh: 可惜天不假年，他没能看到孩子成家。
examples.en: Sadly he did not live long enough to see his child marry.

usage.en: Used in obituaries and elegies; as predicate or comment.
usage.zh: 用于悼念，作谓语或评语。

natural: point straight at the human mind

meaning.en: To go straight to the heart of a matter or to a person's inner nature; in Chan Buddhism, pointing directly at the mind.
meaning.zh: 直接触及人心或事物的核心；禅宗指不借文字，直接指示人的本心。

examples.zh: 这部电影直指人心，让很多观众落了泪。
examples.en: The film goes straight to the heart and moved many viewers to tears.

examples.zh: 好文章要直指人心，而不是堆砌辞藻。
examples.en: A good essay speaks straight to the heart instead of piling up ornate words.

usage.en: Used as predicate or attributive. The Chan phrase 直指人心，见性成佛 describes seeing one's nature directly.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；禅宗有“直指人心，见性成佛”之说。

natural: old in years and weak in strength

meaning.en: To be old and physically weakened.
meaning.zh: 年纪大了，体力衰退。

examples.zh: 他年老力衰，已经干不了重活了。
examples.en: He is old and weak and can no longer do heavy work.

examples.zh: 父母年老力衰，需要子女照顾。
examples.en: The parents are old and frail and need their children's care.

usage.en: Used as predicate or attributive in a plain descriptive tone.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语，语气平实。

natural: young and full of spirit

meaning.en: Young and full of energy and temper, often rash.
meaning.zh: 年纪轻，精力旺盛，容易冲动。

examples.zh: 他年轻气盛，说话常常不留余地。
examples.en: He is young and hot-blooded and often speaks without restraint.

examples.zh: 年轻气盛的时候，我也和人打过架。
examples.en: When I was young and full of beans, I got into fights too.

usage.en: Neutral to slightly critical, often used when excusing youthful rashness.
usage.zh: 中性略含批评，常用于为年轻人的冲动开脱。
